# GitHub CI and Packaging

## Workflows

| Workflow | Trigger | Artifacts and verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CI | Pull requests, pushes to main | Compiles the public source and checks the release contract; separately validates workflow syntax and artifact filtering logic |
| Package (disabled) | None; configuration renamed to `workflows/package.yml.disabled` | Keeps the development package configuration; re-enable by restoring the `.yml` extension |
| Package Sigend | Runs automatically on pushes to main, and can be run manually on main | macOS ARM64 / x64 signing, notarization, and mount verification; artifacts are uploaded only to Actions Artifacts |
| Release | Runs only manually on main, given a Run ID, tag, and channel | Verifies the artifacts of the selected successful build, creates the tag and GitHub Release, does not rebuild |

The signing job uses the existing `ops cd build release --stage installer` direct publishing entry point; it does not call the private distribution repository, does not run OSS uploads, and keeps Actions Artifacts after both architectures pass for later manual publishing; it does not change the private update service version to published. It retains the native lease check plus the builder's signing, notarization, and installation verification; it is not equivalent to the full smoke set of the private distribution workflow.

macOS uses a native build matrix: ARM64 maps to `macos-15`, x64 maps to `macos-15-intel`; each platform is signed, notarized, and mount-verified independently and uploads its own artifact. The x64 build result uses the project architecture name `x86_64`, while the artifact name uses `x64`. GitHub has announced the retirement of macOS 14 hosted runners on 2026-11-02, so new jobs use macOS 15.

The macOS signing job follows the [official temporary workaround for GitHub runners](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14924) to block UDP/443 on the ephemeral runner, forcing Apple ticket queries from unstable HTTP/3 onto HTTPS/TCP. Intel was measured returning 68 from `stapler validate`, and ARM64 also failed to attach the ticket after Accepted, so both architectures use TCP; ticket attachment and validation both log bounded stdout/stderr diagnostics; signing, ticketing, and Gatekeeper checks must still all pass.

## macOS signing configuration

Add Repository secrets under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions:

| Secret | Content |
| --- | --- |
| MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 | Base64 of the `.p12` file containing the Developer ID Application certificate and private key |
| MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD | `.p12` export password |
| APPLE_ID | Apple account with notarization rights for this developer team |
| APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD | App-specific password generated by the same account, not the Apple login password |
| APPLE_TEAM_ID | Apple Developer Team ID that owns the certificate |

The five values are injected only into the check and credential import steps; build steps receive only the Team ID and the keychain profile name. The ephemeral keychain, exported certificate, and notarization credentials live in a temporary directory on the GitHub-hosted runner and are cleaned up at the end. Neither the workspace nor the signing context is uploaded as an artifact.

The update service address comes from `update_base_url` in `apps/desktop/resources/product.json`; the update authorization public key comes from `signing/activation-public-keys.json` and reuses the key already used by existing distributions. That file contains only Ed25519 public keys, no private keys; rotating the authorization key on the server requires a matching review of the update. `preview`/`release` selects the in-package update channel, and both perform production signing and notarization.

Pushing or merging to main automatically runs a preview-channel signed build without creating a tag or Release. To get a production-channel installer, go to Actions → Package Sigend → Run workflow, choose main and the release channel; that operation also only builds and does not publish. This workflow must first land on the default branch before it can be triggered from the UI. Only main can run the signing job; PRs and other branches do not run it. Maintainers who can modify main/workflow can use repository Secrets, so write and review permissions on main should be protected; when independent signing approval is required, repository administrators should migrate to an Environment with approval and branch restrictions.

## Downloading automatically built installers

Open Actions → Package Sigend → the relevant run → Artifacts, and download the `.dmg` for the desired architecture plus the matching `.dmg.sha256`. Ordinary visitors to a public repository can download after signing in to GitHub without repository write permission; unauthenticated users cannot download directly from the Actions page. See the [GitHub artifact download permission documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/download-workflow-artifacts).

Installers, checksum files, and the separate `build-report-*` verification reports are retained for 14 days; installers have no extra ZIP wrapping. When long-term or anonymous downloads are needed, publish manually to a Release.

## Manually publishing a built version

1. Choose a fully successful main build in Package Sigend, download it for trial, and confirm the version. The number after `actions/runs/` in the run page URL is the Run ID.
2. Open Actions → Release → Run workflow, and select main as the branch.
3. Enter that build's `run_id`, a new `tag`, and the in-package `channel`. For example, a preview build can use `v0.3.1-preview.1` and a release build can use `v0.3.1`. Do not create the tag beforehand; the release workflow will point it at the source commit of the selected build.
4. After a successful run, download the same installer from the repository's [Releases](https://github.com/alibaba-damo-academy/ScholarSeed/releases) without rebuilding or re-signing.

- preview can only publish prerelease versions, the tag must start with `v<in-package version>-preview.`, and Latest is not replaced; the release channel uses the `v<in-package version>` production tag. Renaming the tag cannot turn a preview update channel into the production channel.
- The selected run must come from this repository's `signed-macos.yml`, the main branch, a push or manual trigger, and must have fully succeeded. Expired or missing artifacts cannot be published; publish within 14 days or rebuild and test again.
- Before publishing, review the dual-architecture commit, channel, version, build number, signature, notarization, mount verification, and post-download SHA256; the tag points at the build commit, and the Release body links the original build report.
- A Release contains only the two `.dmg` files and their matching `.dmg.sha256`, not `result.json`. The Source code archives that GitHub attaches automatically are source code, not installers.
- After downloading, place the DMG and checksum file in the same directory and run `shasum -a 256 -c <installer file name>.sha256`.
- Only the manual Release job has `contents: write` and `actions: read` and uses the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` by default; signing builds have read-only permissions.
- GitHub imposes an additional permission restriction for historical commits: when the selected commit's `.github/workflows/` differs from the current default branch, creating a Release requires Workflows write permission, which the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot obtain. In that case configure the repository secret `RELEASE_TOKEN`, a fine-grained PAT authorized only for this repository with Contents: write and Workflows: write (the organization may require approval); the release step prefers it. Do not point the tag at another commit to work around the restriction. See the [GitHub Release API permission documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases#create-a-release).
- Existing tags are never overwritten. An interrupted upload may leave an unpublished draft; inspect and clean up that draft before re-running; do not overwrite a published version.

## Windows

The Windows development package matrix entry and build steps are commented out, and Windows packaging does not run for now; uncomment them to restore it. Proper Windows packages still require a project-specific signing client, a reachable signing service, update payload signing, and component distribution configuration; Apple's five secrets do not provide any of these. This change does not mark the Windows development package as a production-signed package.

## Local checks

```bash
actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml
node --test .github/scripts/*.test.cjs
node --test apps/desktop/scripts/cd/__tests__/osx-sign.test.cjs
```

Full source compilation and release contract commands are in `workflows/ci.yml`. Passing syntax, unit tests, or compilation does not mean Apple has accepted notarization; the authoritative evidence of success is a real run of the signing workflow and its `result.json`.

2026-11-03 first integration verification: CI run `41651926527` compiled the source and passed 346 tests; signing run `41651924504` completed Developer ID signing, Apple notarization, DMG mount verification, and artifact upload. The temporarily opened feature-branch entry point from the first trial run has been removed. Signing builds and manual Release publishing have since been split.
